REFRAMED 2026-07-25 by Anthony, and the reframe is the useful part: what he and his brother were asking for is not a staging GATE, it is a KIND. \"I think I now realize what my brother's idea was trying to say — it is like a brainstorming session where you can work through ideas without committing to anything yet. These would be more like 'ideas' not yet fleshed out and could be held in the graph as just that, 'brainstorming ideas'.\" That dissolves the contradiction this decision was opened over. The git study rejected the index because a gate between every edit and the graph is where intent goes to be forgotten; a brainstorm is the opposite move — the idea DOES enter the graph, immediately, labelled as what it is. Nothing waits outside, so nothing is lost, and the design still never claims a half-formed thought as intent. THE QUESTION THAT REMAINS IS THE VOCABULARY ONE, and dec:edge-orthogonality decides it: a distinction earns its keep only if a computation reads it. So what would read `brainstorm`? The candidates, none of them chosen: gap detection must NOT nag about an idea nobody committed to (an unsatisfied brainstorm is not a hole in the design, and today an unsatisfied Requirement fires forever); delivery and certainty counts must exclude it, or the denominator becomes meaningless; promotion must be an explicit human act — a brainstorm becoming a Requirement is the same signature-forging risk dec:certainty-derived guards, one step earlier; and a brainstorm nobody has touched in months is a candidate for retirement rather than an accusation. If none of those is built, the label is decoration and the honest answer is to keep using `proposed` Decisions the way this session already did for the worktree ideas (dec:concurrent-work-isolation). PRIOR FRAMING, KEPT because it is what was true yesterday: the ask read as an opt-in \"think first, commit later\" mode; what already works is that a session making no write calls IS rubber-ducking, and the read tools are the ducking aids; and the narrow question was what happens at the END of such a session — one deliberate commit, with discarded branches either dropped or preserved as unchosen alternatives under a decision point.
